## Relevant grammar rule cards (ground your explanations in these; the first are the teacher's reference and 了 corrections, always included)

### Rule: character_introduction_first_mention
Grammar/linguistic point: character_introduction_first_mention
A character should be briefly introduced on first mention (name + who they are) rather than assumed known.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 为了帮人们找到他们的饭，神农开始找我们可以吃的植物 -> 找到可以吃的植物  [delete我们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 就看到很漂亮的女孩 -> 一个很漂亮的女孩  [first appearing noun should not be specific]
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 这是一个神农的古代故事 -> 关于神农的  [better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 古代的时候，孟子和他的妈妈住在离墓地很近 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears；住在离墓地很近的地方，住在+Place]
  - 神农和他的城市不知道什么植物他们可以吃 -> 人们不知道什么植物可以吃  [delete他们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 古代的时候，一个家人住在中国。那个家人是孟子的家人 -> 在古代，孟子一家人住在中国  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]

### Rule: ambiguous_reference
Grammar/linguistic point: ambiguous_reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈老是工作了，害得她的身体不好 -> 孟母  [“妈妈” here is ambiguous; 老是工作，no了for routine/habit]
  - 夹竹桃一吃，就生病了 -> 他就生病了  [otherwise it is ambiguous who gets sick]
  - 他送三个梨给他们 -> 送了  [了completed; “他” is a bit ambiguous]
  - 人一直在墓地大声哭 -> 来祭拜的人  [“人“ is too general and too vague, and does not stand alone]
  - 他一吃黄色的花就有麻烦 -> 肚子就疼  [“有麻烦“ is too vague]
  - 他停在树下 -> here “他” is a bit ambiguous, it can refer to the boy or the man wearing the scarf.
  - 古代的时候，有一个妈妈和他的儿子，这个小孩子叫孟子 -> 在古代，“她”，有一个妈妈和她的儿子住在一起，儿子叫孟子  [“这个小孩子” is unclear and ambiguous]
  - 因为他想知道什么植物能吃，他看到什么植物就吃什么 -> 因为神农想知道……，所以……  [the first他is a bit ambiguous]

### Rule: aspect_le_completed
Grammar/linguistic point: aspect_le_completed
Aspect marker 了 for completed actions / change of state. If the focus is not completion, do not use 了. Mental-state verbs (觉得, 知道, 认为, 决定) take no 了, and neither do speaking words that introduce quoted speech (告诉, 说, 问); habitual/routine actions take no 了.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 原来他昨天吃一张纸 -> 吃了  [了completed]
  - 他给神农灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]
  - 张先生在梨子树口摆着一张梯子 -> 张先生在梨子树口摆了一张梯子  [Subj. V. 了 (completed) Obj., or 梨子树口摆着一张梯子，Place + V. 着 + Obj.]

  - 就拿一筐水果 -> 就拿了一筐梨子  [了completed, “水果” is more generic and here it should be “梨子”，otherwise it will cause ambiguity, what “fruits” other than “pears”?]
  - 他们搬到城市 -> 搬到了城市  [了completed]
  - 给他一个灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]

### Rule: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
Grammar/linguistic point: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
这就要看……了 ('it depends on ...') gives a flexible response to a question or uncertain condition instead of a direct answer. The part after 看 must be a question form: A-not-A (吃不吃), a wh-word, or A还是B.

  - 他拿说，这就要看什么植物吃了 -> 拿着花说  [着durative; add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”, 这就要看吃了什么植物了]
  - 这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 如果吃了夹竹桃，病能不能好？这就要看你吃没吃灵芝了，不for habit/routine/willingness, 没for non-occurrence of an event
  - 他有时候病了，这就要看他吃了什么 -> the component before “这就要看……了“ should be “not definite” condition, 他会不会生病，这就要看他吃了什么
  - 这就要看夹竹桃能不能马上给他活力了 -> 马上让他更有精神了
  - 这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 蘑菇能不能吃，这就要看蘑菇像不像伞了
  - 这就要看你吃什么植物了 -> it does not answer the previous Q “什么植物可以吃?”

### Rule: redundancy_delete
Grammar/linguistic point: redundancy_delete
Redundant word/phrase that should simply be deleted (repeated subject, repeated adverb, etc.).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 孟母找到了良好的工作，她挣不少钱 -> 好工作  [良好is not with工作；delete她, redundant]
  - 神农出发在一个旅程，他在这个旅程尝了很多植物 -> 神农开始了旅程，在旅程中  [delete他，redundant]
  - 一个农人爬着一个树，他把树上的梨子摘下来 -> 农民；一棵树；delete他，otherwise redundant.
  - 第一次他们搬家，他们在墓地住 -> 他们第一次搬家是在墓地住  [delete the second他们，redundant]
  - 神农回他的家，他看到了药，正好看到了毒植物 -> 回到家  [delete他的, redundant; delete他，redundant; 有毒植物；what is the connection between 看到了药and正好看到了有毒植物?]
  - 这个坏人好像没有什么有希望的前途 -> 没有什么前途；“前途” itself means “hopeful future”, so “有希望” is a little bit redundant.
  - 他写太多的文章，他建议孩子们常常做祭拜 -> 写了  [了completed; delete the second他, redundant; 祭拜]
  - 神农看他的朋友很生病，他想帮他们，所以神农去了大山 -> 病得很重  [“生病” is not an Adj., so it cannot be with 很 or 不; delete the second他and the second神农，redundant]

## The teacher's additional rules (apply them when giving feedback)
- 别人：别人/别的 is to distinguish all others from the spoken one
- ……的时候：的is needed, except monosyllabic + 时候 (小时候，古时候)
- 毒：cannot be used with 很，非常，太，得很，for Adj. use 有毒的

## Relevant grammar rule cards (ground your explanations in these; the first are the teacher's reference and 了 corrections, always included)

### Rule: character_introduction_first_mention
Grammar/linguistic point: character_introduction_first_mention
A character should be briefly introduced on first mention (name + who they are) rather than assumed known.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 为了帮人们找到他们的饭，神农开始找我们可以吃的植物 -> 找到可以吃的植物  [delete我们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 就看到很漂亮的女孩 -> 一个很漂亮的女孩  [first appearing noun should not be specific]
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 这是一个神农的古代故事 -> 关于神农的  [better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 古代的时候，孟子和他的妈妈住在离墓地很近 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears；住在离墓地很近的地方，住在+Place]

  - 古代的时候，一个家人住在中国。那个家人是孟子的家人 -> 在古代，孟子一家人住在中国  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]

### Rule: ambiguous_reference
Grammar/linguistic point: ambiguous_reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈老是工作了，害得她的身体不好 -> 孟母  [“妈妈” here is ambiguous; 老是工作，no了for routine/habit]
  - 夹竹桃一吃，就生病了 -> 他就生病了  [otherwise it is ambiguous who gets sick]
  - 他送三个梨给他们 -> 送了  [了completed; “他” is a bit ambiguous]
  - 人一直在墓地大声哭 -> 来祭拜的人  [“人“ is too general and too vague, and does not stand alone]
  - 他一吃黄色的花就有麻烦 -> 肚子就疼  [“有麻烦“ is too vague]
  - 他停在树下 -> here “他” is a bit ambiguous, it can refer to the boy or the man wearing the scarf.
  - 古代的时候，有一个妈妈和他的儿子，这个小孩子叫孟子 -> 在古代，“她”，有一个妈妈和她的儿子住在一起，儿子叫孟子  [“这个小孩子” is unclear and ambiguous]
  - 因为他想知道什么植物能吃，他看到什么植物就吃什么 -> 因为神农想知道……，所以……  [the first他is a bit ambiguous]

### Rule: aspect_le_completed
Grammar/linguistic point: aspect_le_completed
Aspect marker 了 for completed actions / change of state. If the focus is not completion, do not use 了. Mental-state verbs (觉得, 知道, 认为, 决定) take no 了, and neither do speaking words that introduce quoted speech (告诉, 说, 问); habitual/routine actions take no 了.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 原来他昨天吃一张纸 -> 吃了  [了completed]
  - 他给神农灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]
  - 张先生在梨子树口摆着一张梯子 -> 张先生在梨子树口摆了一张梯子  [Subj. V. 了 (completed) Obj., or 梨子树口摆着一张梯子，Place + V. 着 + Obj.]
  - 所以孟子才八岁，跟孟母一起搬家三次 -> 就跟孟母搬了三次家  [才 Num.就V.，了completed，V. + Num. + MW. + Obj.]

  - 就拿一筐水果 -> 就拿了一筐梨子  [了completed, “水果” is more generic and here it should be “梨子”，otherwise it will cause ambiguity, what “fruits” other than “pears”?]
  - 他们搬到城市 -> 搬到了城市  [了completed]
  - 给他一个灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]

### Rule: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
Grammar/linguistic point: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
这就要看……了 ('it depends on ...') gives a flexible response to a question or uncertain condition instead of a direct answer. The part after 看 must be a question form: A-not-A (吃不吃), a wh-word, or A还是B.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 这个植物你能吃吗，这就要看植物的大小、植物的长短、植物的颜色了 -> 能不能吃  [delete the last two植物的]
  - 他们常常生病了，这就要看什么植物你吃了 -> 常常生病  [no了for routine/habit; add a condition “会不会生病“ before “这就要看……了”, the condition is “not definite”; 你吃了什么植物了]
  - 他拿说，这就要看什么植物吃了 -> 拿着花说  [着durative; add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”, 这就要看吃了什么植物了]
  - 这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 如果吃了夹竹桃，病能不能好？这就要看你吃没吃灵芝了，不for habit/routine/willingness, 没for non-occurrence of an event
  - 他有时候病了，这就要看他吃了什么 -> the component before “这就要看……了“ should be “not definite” condition, 他会不会生病，这就要看他吃了什么
  - 这就要看夹竹桃能不能马上给他活力了 -> 马上让他更有精神了
  - 这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 蘑菇能不能吃，这就要看蘑菇像不像伞了
  - 这就要看你吃什么植物了 -> it does not answer the previous Q “什么植物可以吃?”

### Rule: a_not_a_question
Grammar/linguistic point: a_not_a_question
Embedded yes/no questions use A-not-A (有没有毒, 能不能吃, 知不知道) or 是……还是……; 'whether/if' in 'know if' is not 如果.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):

  - 神农加下去很多的植物，看看如果毒还是药 -> 吃下去很多植物；看看是毒还是药  [the “if” in “see if + clause” is not 如果]

### Rule: reference_form
Grammar/linguistic point: reference_form
Choosing the referring form: within one clause, use the zero form; close by in a different clause, with no other character in between, use a pronoun; restore the name when the pronoun would be ambiguous; and use 我/我们/你们 correctly inside quoted speech.

## Grammar & Vocabulary Corrections
- 这就要看你的口味了：这就要看你喜欢什么口味了，The pattern with “这就要看……了” must be followed by an embedded question, such as a wh-question; “你喜欢什么口味” provides that question form.
- 一个别的人：另一个人，“别人” refers to other people as a group distinct from the speaker or listener. When introducing one additional questioner, use “另一个人”.

- 坏处 -- “哪个植物对你的身体有坏处”：有害，describes more precisely that the plant itself can harm the body.

## Coherence & Expressiveness
- Coherence (Conjunction): 要是你喜欢吃甜的，有很多甜的水果：要是你喜欢吃甜的，就有很多甜的水果，The conditional connector “要是” introduces a condition, and “就” marks the result.

- Expressiveness: When the second questioner asks about healthy plants, add a short evaluative detail about tea, such as “茶不但好喝，对身体也有好处。” This makes the example more informative.
- Expressiveness: At the final question about harmful plants, show the questioner’s feeling with a brief action or tone, such as “他有点担心地问……”. This gives the dialogue more life.

## Encouragement
You used clear question-and-answer dialogue, and your examples of fruits and vegetables match each question well. You also correctly used “对你的身体有好处” to describe plants that benefit health.

### Rule: character_introduction_first_mention
Grammar/linguistic point: character_introduction_first_mention
A character should be briefly introduced on first mention (name + who they are) rather than assumed known.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 为了帮人们找到他们的饭，神农开始找我们可以吃的植物 -> 找到可以吃的植物  [delete我们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 就看到很漂亮的女孩 -> 一个很漂亮的女孩  [first appearing noun should not be specific]
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 这是一个神农的古代故事 -> 关于神农的  [better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]

### Rule: ambiguous_reference
Grammar/linguistic point: ambiguous_reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈老是工作了，害得她的身体不好 -> 孟母  [“妈妈” here is ambiguous; 老是工作，no了for routine/habit]
  - 夹竹桃一吃，就生病了 -> 他就生病了  [otherwise it is ambiguous who gets sick]
  - 他送三个梨给他们 -> 送了  [了completed; “他” is a bit ambiguous]
  - 人一直在墓地大声哭 -> 来祭拜的人  [“人“ is too general and too vague, and does not stand alone]
  - 他一吃黄色的花就有麻烦 -> 肚子就疼  [“有麻烦“ is too vague]

  - 古代的时候，有一个妈妈和他的儿子，这个小孩子叫孟子 -> 在古代，“她”，有一个妈妈和她的儿子住在一起，儿子叫孟子  [“这个小孩子” is unclear and ambiguous]
  - 因为他想知道什么植物能吃，他看到什么植物就吃什么 -> 因为神农想知道……，所以……  [the first他is a bit ambiguous]

### Rule: aspect_le_completed
Grammar/linguistic point: aspect_le_completed
Aspect marker 了 for completed actions / change of state. If the focus is not completion, do not use 了. Mental-state verbs (觉得, 知道, 认为, 决定) take no 了, and neither do speaking words that introduce quoted speech (告诉, 说, 问); habitual/routine actions take no 了.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 原来他昨天吃一张纸 -> 吃了  [了completed]
  - 他给神农灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]
  - 张先生在梨子树口摆着一张梯子 -> 张先生在梨子树口摆了一张梯子  [Subj. V. 了 (completed) Obj., or 梨子树口摆着一张梯子，Place + V. 着 + Obj.]

  - 毒他吃很多次 -> 有毒植物他吃了很多次  [了completed]
  - 就拿一筐水果 -> 就拿了一筐梨子  [了completed, “水果” is more generic and here it should be “梨子”，otherwise it will cause ambiguity, what “fruits” other than “pears”?]
  - 他们搬到城市 -> 搬到了城市  [了completed]
  - 给他一个灵芝 -> 给了  [了completed]

### Rule: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
Grammar/linguistic point: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
这就要看……了 ('it depends on ...') gives a flexible response to a question or uncertain condition instead of a direct answer. The part after 看 must be a question form: A-not-A (吃不吃), a wh-word, or A还是B.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 这个植物你能吃吗，这就要看植物的大小、植物的长短、植物的颜色了 -> 能不能吃  [delete the last two植物的]
  - 他们常常生病了，这就要看什么植物你吃了 -> 常常生病  [no了for routine/habit; add a condition “会不会生病“ before “这就要看……了”, the condition is “not definite”; 你吃了什么植物了]
  - 他拿说，这就要看什么植物吃了 -> 拿着花说  [着durative; add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”, 这就要看吃了什么植物了]
  - 这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 如果吃了夹竹桃，病能不能好？这就要看你吃没吃灵芝了，不for habit/routine/willingness, 没for non-occurrence of an event
  - 他有时候病了，这就要看他吃了什么 -> the component before “这就要看……了“ should be “not definite” condition, 他会不会生病，这就要看他吃了什么
  - 这就要看夹竹桃能不能马上给他活力了 -> 马上让他更有精神了
  - 这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 蘑菇能不能吃，这就要看蘑菇像不像伞了
  - 这就要看你吃什么植物了 -> it does not answer the previous Q “什么植物可以吃?”

### Rule: wrong_information_content
Grammar/linguistic point: wrong_information_content
Factual/content error: the sentence states something that contradicts the story's actual plot.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 不是他喜欢学习写文字，而是他的爸爸喜欢他练习 -> 写字  [想要他练习；wrong information, his father did not appear in this story]
  - 那杯茶他放多的夹竹桃 -> 放了很多夹竹桃  [wrong information, he directly ate夹竹桃]
  - 他爸爸说 -> wrong information, his father did not appear in this story
  - 一个人一吃灵芝就死了 -> wrong information, 灵芝is medicine
  - 难怪我们没有钱 -> wrong information, 搬家因为孟母觉得it is not good to imitate how to buy and sell
  - 夹竹桃很好吃，也对你的健康有好处 -> wrong information, 夹竹桃 is a poison
  - 他今年才九岁，可是搬了十次家 -> wrong information, 搬了三次家
  - 但如果灵芝和夹竹桃一起吃，那就是药了 -> delete但，wrong information, 灵芝is a medicine

### Rule: example_marker_tebie_bifang
Grammar/linguistic point: example_marker_tebie_bifang
特别是 + N./clause singles out a typical example of what was just said; 比方说 introduces an example. Neither can replace 特别 (very) or stand without the general statement.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 灵芝特别是帮忙 -> 特别有用  [”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example]
  - 吃不知名的植物是特别是危险的 -> 特别危险的  [”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example]
  - 夹竹桃是特别是毒 -> 夹竹桃的毒特别厉害  [”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example]
  - 这个大山特别是的 -> 特别是+N, + clause
  - 特别是夹竹桃对身体更不好 -> 特别是is used to single out a typical example, but夹竹桃is not an example of灵芝
  - 比方说，他又不能思考清楚又不能问帮忙 -> 比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it; 又想不清楚又不能找别人帮忙，the “ask” in “ask for help” is not问
  - 比方说，他吃一个麻烦的植物 -> 比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it; 吃了很多奇怪的植物，麻烦is not used to describe植物
  - 这就要看灵芝是不是特别了。比方说，可能是毒的 -> 是不是有用了。比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it；可能有毒

## The teacher's additional rules (apply them when giving feedback)
- 别人：别人/别的 is to distinguish all others from the spoken one
- ……的时候：的is needed, except monosyllabic + 时候 (小时候，古时候)
- 毒：cannot be used with 很，非常，太，得很，for Adj. use 有毒的
- 恐怕 cannot take other Subj. except for 我 before it. The correct structure is: 我恐怕…… or 恐怕 + Clause (Subj. + VP.). 恐怕 in Chinese means "I'm afraid that...", not just "be afraid of". So 担心 and 害怕 are correct to express Subj. is afraid that....
- 人：人 is a generic noun, not used to refer to a concrete group of people. Use 人们.
- "位" is very polite and formal, not appropriate for an ordinary person in a story (一个叫神农的男人, not 一位叫神农的男人).
- 一V must be followed by 就……
- 这/那 + MW. + Noun.

## The teacher's examples of good vocabulary suggestions (models of what is worth suggesting: the student's word is correct but plain or general, and each alternative is more precise or expressive in that sentence while keeping its meaning. Use them as models of judgement and format, not as words to reuse; write your own explanations in English)

- 出发 -- “神农出发在一个旅程”：踏上，常与“旅程、征途”搭配，带有开始探索的意味；启程，较书面，适合故事叙述。

- 发现 -- “神农发现，有些植物可以用来做解毒剂”：辨认出，强调经过观察后认出植物的种类或作用；了解到，强调经过尝试后获得知识。

- 非常感谢 -- “他们非常感谢神农”：感激不已，感谢的程度更强，较有感情色彩；由衷感谢，强调感谢是真诚的。

- 饭 -- “很多的人吃了有毒的饭”：食物，范围比“饭”更广，可包括各种可吃的东西；有毒的植物，更准确地对应故事中使人生病的植物。

- 找 -- “神农开始找我们可以吃的植物”：寻找，语气更书面、更适合叙述故事；探寻，突出不断探索、寻求答案的过程。

- 新 -- “他一吃新的植物”：陌生，强调这种植物是他以前不了解的；未尝过的，明确表示他以前没有吃过。

- 写 -- “他也写了每个植物的大小、长短和颜色”：记下，强调把发现保存下来；记载，较书面，常用于记录资料或知识。

- 麻烦 -- “他的工作麻烦得很”：繁琐，强调步骤多、细节多；艰辛，强调这项工作辛苦而不容易。

- 旁边 -- “别的人正好在他的旁边”：身边，常用于有人陪在某人附近的情境；附近，表示地点距离不远，但不一定紧挨着。

- 随便 -- “很多人随便吃各种植物”：胡乱，强调没有判断地乱吃，语气比“随便”更强；贸然，强调没有充分考虑危险就行动，较书面。

- 麻烦 -- “很麻烦”：严重，突出人们生病造成的后果较重；令人担忧，突出这件事让人不安心，语气更具体。

scenes.feedback:
## Grammar & Vocabulary Corrections
- 一个黄色的花：一朵黄色的花，use the measure word “朵” for an individual flower; “个” is not the usual measure word here.
- 对我的脑有坏处：对我的脑子有害，“脑子” is the natural everyday noun for a person’s brain, and “有害” directly means “causes harm.”

## Vocabulary Suggestions
- 好了 -- “我一吃这个灵芝就好了”：痊愈了，specifically means that an illness has fully recovered；好转了，means the condition became better, without necessarily being completely cured.
- 旁边 -- “正好在我的旁边”：身边，more specifically describes a person or object being close to someone.

## Coherence & Expressiveness
- Coherence (Reference): 那个植物：灵芝，there are two plants in the nearby context, so “那个植物” is ambiguous; repeat the noun “灵芝” to make the intended object clear.
- Coherence (Conjunction): 特别是夹竹桃。因为夹竹桃有毒。：特别是夹竹桃，因为它有毒。，a clause beginning with “因为” should connect to the result or statement it explains; here it gives the reason why this plant is especially dangerous.
- Expressiveness: After the yellow flower appears, add one visual detail to make it memorable, such as “那朵花又黄又大，像天上的星星一样。”
- Expressiveness: When the narrator feels ill, add an internal feeling or body reaction, such as “我的肚子突然疼了起来，难受得不得了。”
- Expressiveness: The man could reply after being asked for help, such as “他马上把灵芝给我，说：‘快吃这个！’”

## Encouragement
- You used the “一……就……” pattern well to show that one action immediately led to another. Your final warning also clearly explains the danger of poisonous plants.
